break_even.method: Per account: membership fee / sample-average (casual ride cost minus member residual). Ceiling gives weak break-even; ties recommend Pay Per Ride/Minute. The strict threshold is floor + 1. Minutes use sample-average billed minutes. This repeated sample-mix approximation is not a guarantee for every ordering of heterogeneous rides.

assumptions: hypothetical assigned account; not observed rider history
Each scenario account purchases its own 30-day membership at coverage_start; fees cannot be shared between accounts.
The coverage end is exclusive for trip starts; every trip must finish within coverage.
Offset-free trip timestamps are interpreted in America/New_York local time; no observed rider identity is inferred.
Pre-tax base transportation comparison: location-dependent sales taxes are excluded.
Parking, damages, lost-bike and other penalties are excluded because the trip CSV does not observe them; ebike totals include transportation only.
Current captured prices are applied counterfactually to the uploaded trip durations.
The entire membership fee is allocated to the calendar week containing coverage_start; later weeks include only residual charges.
Original member_casual describes the public source trip and is not a scenario identity or the product selected for this counterfactual comparison.
A tie recommends Pay Per Ride/Minute; comparison savings are pay-per-use minus membership total.

Each account pays $25 for a 30-day membership with 45 included classic minutes per ride and $0.05 per extra minute [3]. Ride minutes are rounded up separately for every ride [3]. Pay Per Ride/Minute is the recommendation for this assumed 30-day cohort [2][3].

break_even.method: Per account: membership fee / sample-average (casual ride cost minus member residual). Ceiling gives weak break-even; ties recommend Pay Per Ride/Minute. The strict threshold is floor + 1. Minutes use sample-average billed minutes. This repeated sample-mix approximation is not a guarantee for every ordering of heterogeneous rides.

assumptions: hypothetical assigned account; not observed rider history
Each scenario account purchases its own 30-day membership at coverage_start; fees cannot be shared between accounts.
The coverage end is exclusive for trip starts; every trip must finish within coverage.
Offset-free trip timestamps are interpreted in America/New_York local time; no observed rider identity is inferred.
Pre-tax base transportation comparison: location-dependent sales taxes are excluded.
Parking, damages, lost-bike and other penalties are excluded because the trip CSV does not observe them; ebike totals include transportation only.
Current captured prices are applied counterfactually to the uploaded trip durations.
The entire membership fee is allocated to the calendar week containing coverage_start; later weeks include only residual charges.
Original member_casual describes the public source trip and is not a scenario identity or the product selected for this counterfactual comparison.
A tie recommends Pay Per Ride/Minute; comparison savings are pay-per-use minus membership total.
